summary: Eleven comment-endorsed things from the complete prior-day HN front-page comment crawl.
telegram_footer: 11 items surfaced | 30/30 front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated

items.name: Fearless SIMD
items.summary: A Rust SIMD library with safe APIs; users report shipping byte search and FFTs on stable Rust.
items.why_included: Two developers described concrete work enabled by the library, including stable-Rust FFTs.
items.evidence: One developer is happy using it for byte searching; another says it enabled a stable-Rust FFT crate.

evidence_sources.author: Dr_Emann
evidence_sources.excerpt: Have been really happy with Fearless simd, I used it to write

evidence_sources.author: O3marchnative
evidence_sources.excerpt: This is quite amazing. Fearless SIMD is what finally allowed my FFT crate, PhastFT, to run on stable Rust

items.name: SolarOS
items.source_story_title: The newest ESP32 can run Linux and it's getting close to a Raspberry Pi
items.summary: An ESP32 operating environment with Python and Lua runtimes, used to build a handheld PDA.
items.why_included: A user describes a working LilyGO T-Deck project and calls themselves a big fan.
items.evidence: A user runs SolarOS on a LilyGO T-Deck and praises its expanding runtimes and applications.

evidence_sources.author: 100percentjake
evidence_sources.excerpt: a project I've been a big fan of is SolarOS, which provides Python and Lua runtimes for user application development

items.name: COSMIC
items.source_story_title: Ideas on modernizing the open-source desktop
items.summary: A Linux desktop environment whose mixed tiling and floating workflow won over a daily user.
items.why_included: The commenter praises a specific workflow and reports adopting it daily.
items.evidence: A user calls COSMIC's mixed tiling and floating workflow amazing and their new daily driver.

evidence_sources.author: c7b
evidence_sources.excerpt: COSMIC's mixed tiling+floating workflow is amazing and my new daily driver.

items.name: Neo Store
items.summary: A modern F-Droid client suggested as an alternative in the Android app-store discussion.

items.evidence: A commenter recommends trying Neo Store and predicts the reader will like it.

evidence_sources.author: TutleCpt
evidence_sources.excerpt: Check out Neostore too. You'll love it.

items.evidence: The commenter describes Öffi as an excellent public-transit app.

evidence_sources.author: tgsovlerkhgsel
evidence_sources.excerpt: Öffi, an excellent public transit app

items.name: Wander
items.source_story_title: My weird new hobby: Wandering around Tokyo on Google Maps

items.name: The Biology of Cancer
items.source_story_title: Why is the liver so weirdly regenerative?
items.summary: Robert Weinberg's cancer-biology textbook, recommended by a pathologist as an accessible starting point.
items.why_included: A pathologist gives a direct reading recommendation grounded in personal experience.
items.evidence: The pathologist recommends the book as a starting point and calls it their best biological-science read.

evidence_sources.author: 0xWTF
evidence_sources.excerpt: If you really want to learn about this stuff, Robert Weinberg's The Biology of Cancer is where to start.

items.name: Scott Jenson's open-source desktop talk
items.source_story_title: Ideas on modernizing the open-source desktop
items.summary: A talk on rethinking desktop interfaces, praised for its presenter and window-overview demo.
items.why_included: A viewer independently praises the linked talk and cites a specific demo they liked.
items.evidence: A commenter recommends the presenter and liked the demo for moving windows to screen edges.

evidence_sources.author: ardeguire
evidence_sources.excerpt: Scott is a very good presenter, and he clearly thinks about this stuff a lot. I really liked the demo for moving windows to the sides of the screen

items.name: Hyundai Kona Electric
